scope: Proposition 10.2 (Coherent overlap on surviving cells) of the manuscript “Row–column symmetry and contraction of coordinate sweeps” (preprints/Row-column-symmetry-and-contraction-of-coordinate-sweeps-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d27697f3427868fd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M, R, Q ≥ 1 be integers. Consider an M by R grid, n = MR, with l holes and m = n − l surviving cells. Let K, J be the row and column permutation groups on surviving cells. Suppose µ ⊢ m lies in a (Q, Q) hook. For Fourier projections E = N i Eσi,ei and F = N j Eτj,fj selecting one unit carrier vector on each row or column, write σ = (σi) and τ = (τj). Then Dµ TrVµ (EF) ≤ DσDτ exp{l + C(1 + M + R)Q2 log(2n)}. (51) Here Dσ, Dτ denote products over lines, and C is absolute. For m = 0 the surviving representation is the one-dimensional trivial representation.
